subject: On-prem isolation questionnaire & air-gapped option — follow-up
messages:
From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@medatlas.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up from today — vendor questionnaire attached

Camila, thanks again for the call this morning — that was really helpful. Per our discussion we need to qualify the private/on-prem option in more detail before we spin up internal procurement. High-level items we care about: SOC 2 status, GDPR/data residency for EU customers, HIPAA applicability (we will have PHI in production), and an air-gapped deployment option for some regulated sites.

I've attached our standard vendor security questionnaire (MedAtlas_Vendor_Questionnaire.xlsx) — could you confirm a ballpark for turnaround on that? Also, can you send a simple reference network diagram and a checklist of the minimum isolation controls Redwood needs to support an offline/on-prem installation? We want to flag any blockers before legal and security start the procurement flow.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up if helpful.

Tom Alvarez
Director, Platform Operations
MedAtlas Inc.
Alternative contact: elena.rossi@medatlas.com
Attachment: MedAtlas_Vendor_Questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx, 220KB)

Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-30T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — vendor questionnaire attached

Tom — great to chat. Appreciate the clear ring-fenced asks. Quick answers up front: we are SOC 2 Type II in production (attestation available) and have a documented GDPR dataflow model; HIPAA scope depends on whether you route PHI through Redwood-hosted endpoints or run entirely within your VPC/on-prem.

Next steps from our side:
- I'll initiate the questionnaire intake and assign it to our Security Intake queue (ETA 3 business days).
- Neha, can you attach the minimal network template and checklist (drawio + deploy checklist) and add any callouts for air-gap requirements?
- Rishi, please include a short summary of our SOC 2 coverage (controls in-scope) and any compensating controls if MedAtlas requires additional isolation.

If MedAtlas confirms PHI will be present in production, we'll treat this as HIPAA-in-scope and I'll pull in our Compliance lead for a quick readout to legal + your procurement team.

I'll send the intake ticket and a calendar invite for a 30-minute follow-up once we have initial answers.

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: placeholder: initiating questionnaire intake (internal ticket)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-31T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up from today — vendor questionnaire attached

Adding detail from Security:
- SOC 2: Type II attestation file available (we'll link it into the intake ticket). Scope: infra, change management, logical access, monitoring, incident response. Notably, our Private deployments inherit the same controls for the control plane; the customer-managed data plane has documented responsibilities.
- GDPR: We provide region pinning and support EU-only processing. For private VPC, data residency is controlled by deployment region and customer-managed storage.
- HIPAA: If MedAtlas stores/transmits PHI through Redwood-managed endpoints, we require a Business Associate Agreement (BAA). For fully on-prem air-gapped installs where Redwood has no egress, we can operate under a different model but still require baseline documentation and a security review.

Air-gap & network segmentation guidance (summary):
- Minimum segmentation: management plane (control APIs) separated from data plane hosts; no public inbound on data plane nodes; strict egress policies (deny-by-default with required allowlist for support windows).
- Optional hardened flow: physical network separation + jump-hosts for maintenance; dedicated HSM/KMS integration local to customer; periodic offline package delivery for patching.
- Diagram template attached (requested_network_template.drawio) — includes recommended subnets, firewall rules, and suggested NAT/egress controls.

Attachments: requested_network_template.drawio (drawio, 180KB), redwood_private_deploy_checklist.pdf (pdf, 95KB)

I'll draft short answers for the top 12 questionnaire items (control ownership, encryption at rest/in transit, key management, logging retention, incident response SLAs, patching cadence, vulnerability scanning, third-party dependencies, penetration testing cadence, access provisioning, MFA, audit logs). ETA: EOD (next business day).

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Security Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@medatlas.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medatlas.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — vendor questionnaire attached

Camila / Neha — thanks, that level of detail helps a lot. A couple clarifications from our side:
- Confirmed: MedAtlas will have PHI in production (consented clinical notes and imaging metadata). We will need a BAA if any PHI touches Redwood-managed infrastructure.
- For some of our regulated pilot sites (EU and certain Tier-1 hospitals) we need an air-gapped variant — no outbound network, on-site patching windows, and no external KMS unless we can bring our own HSM.

Can you confirm whether your offline package/patch model supports an automated signed bundle we can import? Also please include a short note on how you would audit/verify integrity of deployed runtime in an air-gapped environment (checksums, signed binaries, attestation suggestions).

I'll loop procurement after we get the questionnaire answers. If possible, could you send the completed top-12 answers and the diagram before Wednesday so procurement can start a PR review?

Tom

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@medatlas.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medatlas.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — vendor questionnaire attached

Tom — great, thanks for the confirm on PHI and the air-gap requirements. Action summary & timeline:
1) Security will post top-12 questionnaire answers to the intake ticket by COB today (Neha).
2) Network template + PDF checklist attached to intake (Neha).
3) Rishi will prepare a 1-page SOC 2 coverage summary and flag any gaps for HIPAA/BAA that require legal input (ETA: tomorrow morning).
4) Camila (me) to schedule a 30-min technical readout with MedAtlas + Redwood Security (proposed: 2027-06-03 10:00 PT) — calendar invite to follow.

On your specific asks: offline package model — yes, we support signed offline bundles (sha256 checksums + GPG signatures) and can provide guidance for local verification; we also recommend hardware-backed boot attestation for higher assurance tiers. The checklist includes the verification steps and recommended frequency for integrity checks.

Attachments (in intake): MedAtlas_Vendor_Questionnaire_answers_top12.xlsx (stub), requested_network_template.drawio, redwood_private_deploy_checklist.pdf

If you want, we can include a short example of an offline patch cycle and how Redwood support interacts under a support window (we will provide a proposed SOP for air-gapped maintenance).

Next call will cover: questionnaire walk-through, SOC2/BAA implications, and a draft support SOW for air-gapped pilot.

Thanks — looking forward.

—Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
